Exercise: Hug A Ball

Category:
stretching

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
static

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- glutes
- static_isometric_contraction_of_the_lower_back
- calves

Primary Muscles:

- lower back

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes

Equipment:

- exercise_ball

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
low to moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- improve_spinal_stability
- enhance_core_strength

Contraindications:

- lower back pain
- recent surgery in the lower back or glutes

Exercise Variations:
None

Substitution Options:
None

Instructions:

- Seat yourself on the floor.
- Straddle an exercise ball between both legs and lower your hips down toward the floor.
- Hug your arms around the ball to support your body. Adjust your legs so that your feet are flat on the floor and your knees line up over your ankles. Keep a good grip on the ball so it doesn't roll away from you and send you back onto your buttocks.
